Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to
on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If
applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the
agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk’s office during normal business
hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make
inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be
made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the
Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours
prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however,
to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a
presentation shall be limited to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council must
fill out a green speaker’s card available at the end of each row in the Chambers. The card permits
the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific
agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City
Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of
items shown on the agenda.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA
  April 27, 2010

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 7:30 p.m. in the City Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Humphrey.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL:  Councilmembers Bird, Goodhart, Mayor Pro Tem Rea,
  Mayor Humphrey

ABSENT:  Councilmember Perkins

ALSO PRESENT:  City Manager Hoefgen, City Attorney Hogin, Assistant City
  Manager Smith, Police Chief Dreiling, Public Works Director Rigg,
  City Treasurer Sherwood, Minutes Secretary Monson

CEREMONIAL MATTERS

Police Officer Charles Reed was sworn-in by Chief Dreiling. Officer Reed’s wife, Shelby, pinned on
his badge.

MAYOR’S REPORT – Matters of Community Interest

Mayor Humphrey welcomed new City Attorney Christi Hogin of the law firm Jenkins & Hogin. Ms.
Hogin expressed her appreciation to the City Council and stated that she was looking forward to
serving in the capacity of City Attorney.

Dr. Susan Liberati, Assistant Superintendent of the PVP Unified School District, gave an overview of
enrollment guidelines for students whose parents are employed within the boundaries of the Palos
Verdes Peninsula Unified School District.

CONSENT AGENDA

It was moved by Councilmember Goodhart, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Rea and unanimously
approved that the following Consent Agenda items be approved (Perkins absent):

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Hoefgen reported on the U.S. Census and possible circumstances under which
residents might receive a phone call to verify information provided on their returned census forms.
He also reported that on May 4th on-site workers will begin contacting those premises which had not
returned a census form. Concerned residents may contact City Hall or the Police Department for
more information.

DEMANDS

It was moved by Councilmember Bird and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Rea that the demands, as
approved by a majority of the City Council, totaling $221,563.67 be allowed and it was
unanimously approved. (Perkins absent)

It was moved by Councilmember Bird and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Rea that the demands, as
approved by a majority of the City Council, No. 517181V, 517289V, 517363H to 517367H, 517368
to 517434 totaling $479,665.68 be allowed and it was unanimously approved. (Perkins absent)

MAYOR & CITY COUNCILMEMBERS’ REPORTS

Mayor Humphrey referred Council to the Liaisons to Committees assignments as reflected in the
agenda report.

Councilmember Goodhart reported on the South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG) April
meeting where Bill Allen of the Los Angeles Economic Development Corporation (LAEDC) made a
presentation of the LAC Strategic Plan for Economic Development for 2010-2014. The plan was
unanimously endorsed by the SBCCOG.

Councilmember Goodhart reported that the City of Gardena has implemented a prescription drug
collection program. He said Gardena has reported the response to the program has been extraordinary.
